column1: # Upstream support status for Kryptik's pinned release series.
# Read by tools/check-support-status.sh.
# Every row records WHERE the claim came from and WHEN it was read, because a
# support date with no source is a rumour and a support date with no retrieval
# date rots silently into one.
# Columns are whitespace separated; the note runs to the end of the line.
#   package       source name, as in sources.lock and tools/fetch-sources.sh
#   config_var    the pin in build/config/versions.env
#   series        the release series this row describes, or * for any series
#   status        supported | security-only | none-published | delegated
#   support_ends  YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when upstream publishes only a month,
#                 or - when upstream publishes a support tier and not a date
#   policy_url    the upstream page this row was read from
#   retrieved     the date it was read
#   note          free text
# What the statuses mean:
#   supported       upstream supports the series; support_ends says until when.
#                   Some projects publish a TIER instead of a calendar date --
#                   perlpolicy names the two most recent stable series and
#                   calls every older one end of life. Leave support_ends as -
#                   for those and record the tier in the note. Such a row can
#                   never expire on its own, which is precisely why it must say
#                   what it was read from; the note is required, not optional.
#   security-only   upstream ships security fixes only for this series. Still
#                   supported, so this is a warning and not a failure, but it
#                   is the last stop before end of life.
#   none-published  upstream publishes NO version-based support window at all.
#                   This is a RECORDED FACT AND NOT A STATEMENT THAT THE PIN
#                   IS CURRENT. A package can be twenty security releases
#                   behind and still sit honestly on this row. Currency is
#                   tools/check-source-currency.sh's question, not this file's.
#   delegated       support status is established by another tool, named in the
#                   note. --strict requires that tool to exist, because a
#                   delegation to something absent is a skipped check, and a
#                   skipped check is not a pass.
# A pinned series with no row here is reported as off the policy map and fails
# --strict. That is deliberate: moving a pin to a series nobody has looked up
# should require looking it up. Add the row from upstream's own page.
# DO NOT populate this file from a distribution's security tracker or a
# third-party end-of-life aggregator. Those are someone else's summary of
# upstream, and when the summary is wrong this file becomes confidently wrong
# in the one place a reader would trust it.
# package  config_var   series  status          support_ends  policy_url                                            retrieved   note
